summary:
We developed Estación Selene, a Unity game that puts players in charge of a lunar research station for 15 days. With only three tasks per day, players must decide when to restore oxygen, grow food, clean solar panels, or send research reports to Earth. Those decisions affect the station’s resources and the astronaut’s stress, and a nightly journal records the consequences.

The game addresses the challenge of making space science accessible through hands-on exploration. Players can read about real solar flares from NASA’s DONKI archive and use a NASA Mars Trek terrain mosaic to locate Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, and Olympus Mons. Three optional training modules let players experiment with solar power, collect a sample with a rover, and align an antenna to transmit an observation.

Estación Selene helps players understand how astronaut safety, equipment maintenance, and scientific work depend on one another when supplies and time are limited.
